- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Code: _load_lessons_learned_records, called from select_lessons_for_context, called from retrieve_memory_context.
  Problem: every retrieval call iterates sorted(task_root.glob("*/lessons_learned/*.json")) and runs JSON-load + schema-validate on every record, even though the function caps the output at LESSONS_RETRIEVAL_MAX (5). For repos with many orchestrator projects (each appending one retrospective record per completion), this becomes O(N) per retrieve, and retrieve is called from every plan / implement / review prompt.
  Why it fails at runtime: a single workflow run that issues, say, three retrieves now performs N file reads + N JSON parses + N schema validations three times. The plan/implementation/reviewer fan-out in review_autofix.yml alone can multiply this. There is no caching across calls in the same process, no limit on how many lessons are loaded before sort-and-trim, and no early-exit when the cap has been reached (the function returns ALL valid records sorted by discovered_at, then truncates).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (record_orchestrator_lesson_event, around line 455-466)
  Code:
    if ! PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 scripts/orchestrate_lib.py append-lesson-event \
      --state-file "${STATE_FILE}" --event-json "${event_json}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "::warning::tracking #${TRACKING_NUM:-?}: could not record orchestrator lesson event; continuing fail-open" >&2
    fi
  Issue: the Python process's stdout AND stderr are both redirected to /dev/null, so the warning message carries no diagnostic context (just "could not record"). When the warning fires repeatedly in a tick (e.g. several judge_fixup events fail), operators have nothing to grep for beyond "could not record". The fail-open contract is correct, but a one-line fix to capture and forward the exception message would not change the contract.
  Suggested minimal fix: redirect only stdout to /dev/null and capture the last line of stderr into the warning (`2>/tmp/.lerr` then `awk` or similar), or write a one-liner `--format json` shim that emits `{ok: false, error: "..."}` for fail-open consumers to log.
  Estimated lines changed: ~3
